reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment helpers, but implements daily skip-versus-move policy separately in shared scheduling, both handlers, and budget templates.

duplication.why: Daily recurrence policy is repeated across three consumer blocks, and daily occurrence searches independently encode their stopping limits.

placement.why: Holiday matching belongs appropriately in shared schedules, but frequency-dependent scheduling policy leaks into server handlers and budget template calculations.

scope.why: The edits are focused on the requested scheduling changes, their data propagation, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Centralized holiday matching helps, but scattered daily-policy branches, independent search bounds, and an untyped handler config make future rule changes harder to maintain.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getDatesInRange and getUpcomingDates implement daily occurrence filtering outside getNextDate, while createScheduleList computes frequency-dependent switches around the shared weekend helpers.

disguised_duplication.where: The daily skip-versus-move decision appears as a shared-helper dispatch, handler filtering loops, and frequency-derived boolean arguments in budget templates.

abstraction_drift.where: Holiday inputs extend getDateWithSkippedWeekend and WeekendRule; getNextDate gains a daily special case, while getDatesInRange, getUpcomingDates, and createScheduleList independently encode parts of that policy.
